items.title: Finite-state discounted generator Bellman system
items.strategy: Define the finite nonempty state set, finite ordered nonempty actions, conservative generator rows, rewards, positive discount, Bellman equation, and policy matrix.

references.title: Wang He, Reinforcement Learning: A Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 10, Policy Improvement and Policy Iteration
references.locator: §§10.2–10.9: finite discounted policy evaluation, greedy improvement, and policy iteration.

items.statement:
Let $S=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a nonempty finite state set, let each state $i$
have a nonempty finite ordered action set $A_i$, and let $c>0$. For
$a\in A_i$, choose real coefficients $q^a_{ij}$ satisfying
$$q^a_{ij}\ge0\quad(j\ne i),\qquad \sum_{j=1}^nq^a_{ij}=0,$$
and a reward $r_i^a\in\mathbb R$. The row $q_i^a$ is a conservative generator
row. A deterministic policy is a map $\pi$ with $\pi(i)\in A_i$. Its policy
matrix and reward vector are
$$A^\pi_{ij}=c\,\delta_{ij}-q^{\pi(i)}_{ij},\qquad r^\pi_i=r_i^{\pi(i)}.$$
The **discounted finite-state Bellman system** is
$$cV_i-\max_{a\in A_i}\left(\sum_{j=1}^nq^a_{ij}V_j+r_i^a\right)=0, \qquad i\in S.$$
The policy evaluation equation for $\pi$ is $A^\pi V=r^\pi$.

Here $\delta_{ij}$ is $1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.

items.title: Second-order elliptic semijets and their value-sensitive closures
items.strategy: not-applicable

references.title: Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: Sections 2–3 and Appendix A, printed pp. 9–18 and 56–63.

items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, $u:U\to\mathbb R$, and $z\in U$. Write $\mathbb S^m$ for the real symmetric $m$ by $m$ matrices. The second-order elliptic superjet consists of pairs $(p,X)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^m$ such that
$$u(z+h)\le u(z)+p\cdot h+\tfrac12 h^{\mathsf T}Xh+o(|h|^2)\quad(h\to0).$$
Here the inequality means that its positive remainder divided by $|h|^2$ has limit zero. Denote this set by $J^{2,+}u(z)$. Define
$$J^{2,-}u(z)=-J^{2,+}(-u)(z).$$
The closed superjet $\overline J^{2,+}u(z)$ consists of all limits $(p,X)$ for which there are $z_n\in U$ and $(p_n,X_n)\in J^{2,+}u(z_n)$ satisfying
$$(z_n,u(z_n),p_n,X_n)\longrightarrow(z,u(z),p,X).$$
Define $\overline J^{2,-}u(z)=-\overline J^{2,+}(-u)(z)$. The value convergence is part of the definition. The same definitions work for functions allowed to equal $-\infty$ away from the finite base point, with all approximating base values finite. A two-sided quadratic expansion means that both the upper and lower inequalities hold with the same $(p,X)$; it is also called a second-order Peano expansion. Matrix order means $X\le Y$ iff $h^{\mathsf T}Xh\le h^{\mathsf T}Yh$ for every $h$.

For space-time $z=(t,x)$ this is the full Euclidean jet, whose matrix also has time and mixed entries. No assertion about parabolic jets is included in this definition.

items.title: Convex supports, localization, and the Lipschitz dual gradient
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces, complete 168-page notes; Sections 2.6 and 3.3-3.4
Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions, Appendix A, Theorem A.2 and pp. 58-60, notes pp. 62-63

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $f$ be finite convex, in the sense of [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]], on an open convex $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. At each $x\in U$ the subdifferential $\partial f(x)=\{p:f(y)\ge f(x)+p\cdot(y-x)\ (y\in U)\}$ is nonempty; it is locally bounded and its graph is locally closed. It is a singleton exactly when $f$ is differentiable, and then equals $\{Df(x)\}$. For every closed Euclidean ball $K\subset U$ ([[def-metric-ball]]) there is a finite globally Lipschitz convex $H$ ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]]) on $\mathbb R^n$ equal to $f$ on $K$. For $F(x)=H(x)+|x|^2/2$, the conjugate $F^*(p)=\sup_x(p\cdot x-F(x))$ is finite and $C^1$, and $g=DF^*$ is globally one-Lipschitz with $g(p)=x$ iff $p\in\partial F(x)$.

items.title: Jensen maximum principle for locally semiconvex functions
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: Sections 2–3 and Appendix A, printed pp. 9–18 and 56–63.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $f$ be finite and locally semiconvex near $0\in\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge1$: on some Euclidean ball ([[def-metric-ball]]), $f(x)+\lambda|x|^2/2$ is convex ([[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]) for a finite $\lambda\ge0$. Suppose $0$ is a strict local maximum of $f$. For every sufficiently small $r>0$ and every $\delta>0$, the set of points $x\in B_r(0)$ where $f(x)+q\cdot x$ has a local maximum for some $|q|\le\delta$ contains a compact subset of positive Lebesgue outer measure. Consequently, given any Lebesgue null set $N$, such a maximum can be chosen with $x\notin N$, $|x|<r$, and $|q|\le\delta$.

items.title: Critical images of Euclidean Lipschitz maps are null
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces, complete 168-page notes; Sections 2.6 and 3.3-3.4

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ be $L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]]), where $n\ge1$. Write $B(x,r)$ for the Euclidean ball ([[def-metric-ball]]). Let
$$C=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:g(p+h)=g(p)+Dg(p)h+o(|h|)\text{ as }h\to0,\ \det Dg(p)=0\}.$$
Then $g(C)$ is null in $\mathbb R^n$.

items.strategy: direct

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces, complete 168-page notes; Sections 2.6 and 3.3-3.4

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and locally Lipschitz map $u:U\to\mathbb R^m$ (each point has a neighborhood on which $|u(y)-u(z)|\le L|y-z|$ for some finite $L$, [[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]]), $u$ is Frechet differentiable outside a null subset of $U$. Here Frechet differentiability at $x$ means that a linear map $A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ satisfies $u(x+h)=u(x)+Ah+o(|h|)$.

items.title: Periodic Cartesian grids and tensor-product multilinear interpolation
items.strategy: Define the quotient torus, periodic grid indices, mesh conventions, and the explicit multilinear weights on each cell.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: Section 2, conditions (I1)–(I2), printed pp. 2–3: interpolation accuracy and nonnegative nodal weights.

items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and integers $N_j\ge3$, $1\le j\le d$. This is the
unit-period specialization of the periodic tensor-grid definition in
[[def-semilagrangian-periodic-grid-and-interpolant]], with each period
$\ell_j=1$. Put
$h_j=1/N_j$ and define the periodic unit torus as
$\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$; functions on it are identified with
$\mathbb Z^d$-periodic functions on $\mathbb R^d$. The Cartesian grid has nodes
$$x_i=(i_1h_1,\ldots,i_dh_d)\pmod{\mathbb Z^d},\qquad i_j\in\{0,\ldots,N_j-1\}.$$
Indices on nodal arrays are always reduced modulo $N_j$ in coordinate $j$.

For a nodal array $V=(V_i)$ and $x$ in the cell with lower corner $x_i$, write
$\widetilde x_j=(i_j+\theta_j)h_j$ in a periodic lift, where
$0\le\theta_j\le1$.
Write $I_h$ for the supplier's tensor-product multilinear interpolant. In
the local coordinates above, it is
$$I_hV(x)=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^d} \left(\prod_{j=1}^d\theta_j^{\epsilon_j}(1-\theta_j)^{1-\epsilon_j}\right)V_{i+\epsilon}.$$
At cell faces either adjacent cell formula gives the same value, because the
weight of the opposite face is zero. The formula is periodic and therefore
defines $I_hV$ on $\mathbb T^d$.

In dimension two the four nodal weights on one cell are shown below. The dot is
the evaluation point; the labels are exactly the four factors in the formula.
The diagram fixes the cell convention only; no later proof relies on it.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1.1]
  \draw (0,0) rectangle (3,2);
  \fill (1.2,0.8) circle (1.5pt);
  \node[below left] at (0,0) {$V_{00}$};
  \node[below right] at (3,0) {$V_{10}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,2) {$V_{01}$};
  \node[above right] at (3,2) {$V_{11}$};
  \node[below] at (1.5,-0.35) {$(1-\theta_1,\,\theta_1)$};
  \node[left] at (-0.45,1) {$(1-\theta_2,\,\theta_2)$};
  \node[above right] at (1.2,0.8) {$x$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

items.statement:
For every policy $\pi$ in [[def-na-finite-state-discounted-bellman-system]],
the matrix $A^\pi=cI-Q^\pi$ is nonsingular, $(A^\pi)^{-1}$ is entrywise

items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty compact, let $v:K\to\mathbb R$ be upper semicontinuous (so $\limsup_{y\to x}v(y)\le v(x)$ for each $x\in K$), and extend $v$ by $-\infty$ off $K$. For $\lambda>0$ define
$$\widehat v(\xi)=\max_{x\in K}\{v(x)-\tfrac\lambda2|x-\xi|^2\}.$$
This is finite, continuous and $\lambda$-semiconvex on $\mathbb R^m$, meaning that $\widehat v(\xi)+\lambda|\xi|^2/2$ is convex ([[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]). If $(q,Y)\in J^{2,+}\widehat v(\eta)$, every maximizing point equals $y=\eta+q/\lambda$, and
$$(q,Y)\in J^{2,+}v(y),\qquad v(y)=\widehat v(\eta)+\frac{|q|^2}{2\lambda}.$$
The jets of $v$ are understood for its extended function, or for its original local domain if $y$ is interior to $K$. These conclusions use no choice principle.

items.strategy: direct

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces, complete 168-page notes; Sections 2.6 and 3.3-3.4

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and let $u:U\to\mathbb R$ be locally semiconvex: around each point there is a Euclidean ball ([[def-metric-ball]]) and $c\ge0$ such that $x\mapsto u(x)+c|x|^2/2$ is convex in the sense of [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]. Outside a set null in the cube-cover sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]], there are $p\in\mathbb R^n$ and a symmetric matrix $A$ with
$$u(x+h)=u(x)+p\cdot h+\tfrac12h^{\mathsf T}Ah+o(|h|^2)\quad(h\to0).$$
The remainder is uniform in direction. In particular $u$ is twice differentiable in the Peano sense almost everywhere.

items.title: Finite-budget Howard policy iteration for a discounted generator Bellman system
items.strategy: Define exact policy solves, strict-improvement states, least-index maximizing switches, deterministic tie retention, budget exhaustion, and the finite policy-count budget.

references.title: Wang He, Reinforcement Learning: A Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 10, Policy Improvement and Policy Iteration
references.locator: §§10.6–10.9: policy improvement, exact policy iteration, deterministic ties, and finite termination.

items.statement:
For the finite system of [[def-na-finite-state-discounted-bellman-system]],
order each finite set $A_i$ by its declared indices and put
$P=\prod_{i\in S}|A_i|$. The procedure takes a positive integer evaluation
budget $K\in\mathbb N$, $K\ge1$ (default $K=P$), and proceeds as follows.

1. Initialize $\pi_0(i)$ to the least-index action in $A_i$.
2. For the current policy $\pi_k$, solve exactly
   $A^{\pi_k}V^k=r^{\pi_k}$.
3. Form the strict-improvement set
   $$J_k=\left\{i:\max_{a\in A_i}(Q_i^aV^k+r_i^a)>Q_i^{\pi_k(i)}V^k+r_i^{\pi_k(i)}\right\},$$
   where $Q_i^aV=\sum_jq^a_{ij}V_j$.
4. If $J_k=\varnothing$, return $(\texttt{converged},\pi_k,V^k)$.
5. If $J_k\ne\varnothing$ and $k+1=K$, return
   $(\texttt{budget\_exhausted},\pi_k,V^k)$; this status makes no Bellman-solution
   claim.
6. Otherwise, at each $i\in J_k$ switch to the least-index maximizing action
   in $A_i$; retain $\pi_k(i)$ at every state outside $J_k$ and continue.

The policy matrix solve is well-defined by
[[lem-na-discounted-bellman-policy-matrix-inverse-positive]]. A budget of $P$
policy evaluations is sufficient by the theorem below.

items.title: Periodic first-order controlled Hamilton–Jacobi Cauchy problem
items.strategy: Fix the periodic unit torus, compact or finite controls, coefficient hypotheses, Hamiltonian sign, initial data, and control-grid error convention.

references.title: Hung Vinh Tran, Hamilton–Jacobi Equations: Theory and Applications, 2020 author manuscript
references.locator: Chapter 1 §§1–6, especially the first-order Cauchy problem and comparison theorem, printed pp. 9–29.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §1, controlled first-order and second-order HJB Cauchy equations, printed pp. 1–2.

items.statement:
Let $d,q\ge1$, $T>0$, and let $A$ be a nonempty compact subset of
$\mathbb R^q$ (a finite action set is included). For each $a\in A$, let
$b_a:\mathbb T^d\times[0,T]\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$\ell_a:\mathbb T^d\times[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and jointly
continuous in $(x,t,a)$. Write $b_a,\ell_a$ also for their periodic lifts to
$\mathbb R^d\times[0,T]$. Assume there are constants $B,L<\infty$ such that
$$|b_a(x,t)|\le B,\qquad |\ell_a(x,t)|\le L,$$
and for all $a\in A$, $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$, and $t,s\in[0,T]$,
$$|b_a(x,t)-b_a(y,s)|+|\ell_a(x,t)-\ell_a(y,s)| \le L(|x-y|+|t-s|).$$
Given continuous periodic initial data $u_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$, define
$$H(x,t,p)=\max_{a\in A}\{-b_a(x,t)\cdot p-\ell_a(x,t)\}.$$
The **periodic first-order controlled Hamilton–Jacobi Cauchy problem** is
$$u_t+H(x,t,Du)=0\quad\text{on }\mathbb T^d\times(0,T),\qquad u(x,0)=u_0(x).$$
The signs are fixed by
$u_t=\min_{a\in A}\{b_a\cdot Du+\ell_a\}$. Whenever the controls are
discretized, use a sequence of finite nonempty sets $A_k\subseteq A$ and define
$$H_k(x,t,p):=\max_{a\in A_k}(-b_a\cdot p-\ell_a).$$
Define the Hamiltonian error by
$$\eta_k(R):=\sup_{x,t,|p|\le R}|H_k(x,t,p)-H(x,t,p)|.$$
The sequence is admissible when $\eta_k(R)\to0$ for every $R<\infty$.
Exact minimization over $A$ corresponds to $\eta_k=0$. Scheme convergence below
uses this explicit control-grid error whenever the controls are discretized.

items.title: Periodic diagonal controlled-diffusion HJB Cauchy problem
items.strategy: Define the finite-control periodic PDE, uniformly positive diagonal diffusion and bounded Lipschitz coefficients, initial data, and exact sign convention.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and let $A$ be a nonempty finite ordered control set.
For each $a\in A$ and $j=1,\ldots,d$, let
$\alpha_j^a,b_j^a,f^a:\mathbb T^d\times[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and
periodic, jointly continuous in $(x,t)$, and uniformly Lipschitz in $(x,t)$.
Assume a common constant $\alpha_*>0$ satisfies
$$\alpha_j^a(x,t)\ge\alpha_*\qquad\text{for every }a,j,x,t.$$
The **diagonal controlled-diffusion HJB Cauchy problem** is
$$u_t-\max_{a\in A}\left\{ \sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(\alpha_j^a(x,t)u_{x_jx_j}+b_j^a(x,t)u_{x_j}\bigr)+f^a(x,t) \right\}=0\quad\text{on }\mathbb T^d\times(0,T),$$
with continuous periodic initial data $u(x,0)=u_0(x)$. In the convention
$u_t+F(x,t,Du,D^2u)=0$, this has
$$F(x,t,p,X)=-\max_{a\in A}\left\{ \sum_j(\alpha_j^a X_{jj}+b_j^a p_j)+f^a\right\},$$
which is nonincreasing in each diagonal Hessian entry. No off-diagonal
diffusion or arbitrary anisotropic central stencil is covered.

items.statement:
For the interpolant $I_h$ of [[def-na-periodic-grid-and-tensor-multilinear-interpolation]], every cell weight is nonnegative and the weights sum to one by
[[lem-periodic-tensor-interpolant-is-convex-and-linf-contracting]]. Hence
$V\le W$ on grid nodes implies $I_hV\le I_hW$, and
$\|I_hV\|_{\infty}\le\|V\|_{\infty}$. If $\phi\in C^2(\mathbb T^d)$ and $V_i=\phi(x_i)$, then
$$\|I_hV-\phi\|_{\infty}\le\frac18\sum_{j=1}^d h_j^2\|\partial_{jj}\phi\|_{\infty}.$$

items.title: Elliptic theorem of sums with the full block matrix bound
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: Sections 2–3 and Appendix A, printed pp. 9–18 and 56–63.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $n_i\ge1$, let $U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}$ be open, and let $u_i:U_i\to\mathbb R$ be upper semicontinuous, meaning $\limsup_{y\to x}u_i(y)\le u_i(x)$ at each $x\in U_i$. Suppose $\phi$ is $C^2$ near $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)\in\prod_iU_i$ and $\sum_i u_i(x_i)-\phi(x)$ has a local maximum at $z$. Set $A=D^2\phi(z)$, and let $\|A\|$ be its Euclidean operator norm ([[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]). For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $X_i\in\mathbb S^{n_i}$ such that
$$(D_i\phi(z),X_i)\in\overline J^{2,+}u_i(z_i),$$
and
$$-\left(\varepsilon^{-1}+\|A\|\right)I\ \le\ \operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_k)\ \le\ A+\varepsilon A^2.$$
Here all jets are full Euclidean jets. In particular one may take each $U_i$ to be a space-time domain of dimension $d+1$. For a lower semicontinuous function $v$, applying the theorem to $-v$ and then negating its jet gives the corresponding closed subjet for $v$.

items.title: Explicit monotone diagonal-diffusion Bellman grid update
items.strategy: Define the periodic second-difference and sign-selected one-sided drift stencils, control maximum, diffusion-dominance condition, and explicit CFL.

items.statement:
Use the model of [[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]] and a periodic grid with integers $N_j\ge3$, $h_j=1/N_j$. Choose an integer $M\ge1$, set $\tau=T/M$, and put $t_n=n\tau$ for $n=0,\ldots,M$. For a nodal array $V$, define
$$D_{jj}^hV_i=\frac{V_{i+e_j}-2V_i+V_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.$$
For a control $a$, define
$$D_{j,a}^{up}V_i=\begin{cases}(V_i-V_{i-e_j})/h_j,&b_j^a(x_i,t_n)\ge0,\\(V_{i+e_j}-V_i)/h_j,&b_j^a(x_i,t_n)<0.\end{cases}$$
The recurrence is
$$U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n+\tau\max_{a\in A}\left\{\sum_{j=1}^d\left[\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n)D_{jj}^hU_i+b_j^a(x_i,t_n)D_{j,a}^{up}U_i\right]+f^a(x_i,t_n)\right\}.$$
At each time level $n=0,\ldots,M-1$, admit the update only when, at every node, control, and coordinate,
$$|b_j^a(x_i,t_n)|h_j\le\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n),$$
and
$$\tau\max_{i,a}\sum_{j=1}^d\left(\frac{2\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n)}{h_j^2}+\frac{|b_j^a(x_i,t_n)|}{h_j}\right)\le1.$$
Initialize by $U_i^0=u_0(x_i)$ and perform the updates for $n=0,\ldots,M-1$, evaluating coefficients at $(x_i,t_n)$. Return $U^M$. No claim about an arbitrary anisotropic central stencil is included.

items.title: Positive-interpolation semi-Lagrangian update for first-order HJB equations
items.strategy: Specify initial sampling, periodic wrapping, the finite controlled update, exact-minimization or finite-control error input, and output.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §§2–4, positive interpolation and semi-Lagrangian HJB updates, printed pp. 2–5.

items.statement:
Choose integers $N_j\ge3$, a number $M\ge1$ of time steps, and
$\tau=T/M$. Sample $u_0$ at the grid nodes of
[[def-na-periodic-grid-and-tensor-multilinear-interpolation]] and set
$U_i^0=u_0(x_i)$. At each $n=0,\ldots,M-1$, compute
$$U_i^{n+1}=\min_{a\in A_k}\left\{ I_hU^n\bigl(x_i+\tau b_a(x_i,t_n)\bigr)+\tau\ell_a(x_i,t_n) \right\},\qquad t_n=n\tau.$$
The position is evaluated on the torus, so its coordinates wrap modulo one.
The algorithm always uses a finite nonempty set $A_k\subset A$. For a finite
control model take $A_k=A$; for a compact control model, supply finite sets
whose Hamiltonian errors $\eta_k(R)$ from
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]] tend to zero on every bounded
momentum set. This is the declared finite-control approximation branch; it
does not presume an unimplemented continuous minimization oracle. Return
$U^M$.

The update is the explicit Euler-footpoint semi-Lagrangian branch specified by
the plan. It defines its footpoint and interpolant locally; no unauthored
characteristic-flow estimate is presumed.

items.title: CFL-monotone upwind update for first-order HJB equations

items.statement:
Use the model and coefficient notation of [[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]] and the periodic grid of [[def-na-periodic-grid-and-tensor-multilinear-interpolation]]. Choose an integer $M\ge1$, set $\tau=T/M$, and put $t_n=n\tau$ for $n=0,\ldots,M$. Choose a finite nonempty control set $A_k\subseteq A$. For a finite control model take $A_k=A$; for compact controls use a sequence of finite nonempty sets with the stated uniform Hamiltonian error. For each control and grid node put
$$b_{a,j}^+=\max\{b_{a,j},0\},\qquad b_{a,j}^- =\max\{-b_{a,j},0\},$$
and define the explicit row
$$G^a_i(V)=V_i+\tau\left[\sum_{j=1}^d\left(\frac{b_{a,j}^+(x_i,t_n)}{h_j}(V_{i+e_j}-V_i)+\frac{b_{a,j}^-(x_i,t_n)}{h_j}(V_{i-e_j}-V_i)\right)+\ell_a(x_i,t_n)\right].$$
The periodic HJB upwind update at time $t_n$ is
$$U_i^{n+1}=\min_{a\in A_k}G_i^a(U^n).$$
At every step $n=0,\ldots,M-1$, require the CFL condition
$$\tau\max_{a,i}\sum_{j=1}^d\frac{|b_{a,j}(x_i,t_n)|}{h_j}\le1$$
Initialize $U_i^0=u_0(x_i)$ and perform the updates for $n=0,\ldots,M-1$. Return $U^M$. Since the transport velocity in [[def-periodic-one-way-advection-schemes]] is $-b_a$ for this Hamiltonian sign convention, the displayed one-sided direction is its sign-reflected upwind row.

items.title: Second-order parabolic viscosity subsolutions and supersolutions
items.strategy: Extend the local maximum/minimum test convention to C^{1,2} test functions and the diagonal controlled-diffusion operator.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §2 viscosity definitions and §8 parabolic problems, printed pp. 9–13 and 49–52.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §1, second-order viscosity subsolution and supersolution definition, printed pp. 272–274.

items.statement:
Let $u$ be upper semicontinuous and $v$ lower semicontinuous on the periodic
space-time cylinder. A **second-order parabolic viscosity subsolution** of
[[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]] is a function $u$
such that every $C^{1,2}$ test function $\phi$ for which $u-\phi$ has a local
maximum at $(x_0,t_0)$, $0<t_0<T$, satisfies
$$\phi_t(x_0,t_0)-\max_{a\in A}\left\{\sum_j\left(\alpha_j^a\phi_{x_jx_j}+b_j^a\phi_{x_j}\right)(x_0,t_0)+f^a(x_0,t_0)\right\}\le0.$$
Here $C^{1,2}$ means that $\phi_t$, all first spatial derivatives, and all
second spatial derivatives exist and are continuous near the contact point.
A **supersolution** is lower semicontinuous and satisfies the reverse
inequality at every local minimum. A viscosity solution is both. For the Cauchy
problem, the relaxed initial conditions are
$$\limsup_{(y,s)\to(x,0),\ s>0}u(y,s)\le u_0(x),\qquad \liminf_{(y,s)\to(x,0),\ s>0}v(y,s)\ge u_0(x).$$

items.title: Localization of strict half-relaxed contacts to periodic mesh nodes
items.strategy: Use the set-defined half-relaxed envelope to recover near-contact points, replace interpolant values by a nodal value, then maximize on a finite grid in a strict-contact ball and exclude its annulus by compactness.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §6, half-relaxed limits; Appendix A strict-contact and approximation arguments, printed pp. 34–35 and 56–63.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2 proof of Theorem 2.1, strict contact and mesh-maximizer localization, printed pp. 275–276.

items.statement:
Let $V_k$ be locally bounded periodic interpolant extensions of finite nodal
arrays on grids with $h_k\to0$ and time steps $\tau_k\to0$. Regard this
sequence as the family $V_\epsilon=V_k$ when
$(k+1)^{-1}<\epsilon\le k^{-1}$, and form its upper and lower half-relaxed
limits as in
[[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. If $\overline V-\phi$ has a strict local maximum
at an interior point $z_0=(x_0,t_0)$ for a smooth test $\phi$, then there are
mesh indices $k_m\to\infty$ and grid points $z_m=(x_{i_m},t_{n_m})\to z_0$
such that $V_{k_m}(z_m)-\phi(z_m)\to\overline V(z_0)-\phi(z_0)$ and $z_m$ is
a local maximum of the corresponding nodal values minus $\phi$ on a fixed
closed space-time ball. The lower half-relaxed limit has the dual strict
minimum property. The proof uses Countable Choice only for sequential recovery
from the set-defined half-relaxed limit.

items.title: Monotone improvement and finite termination of exact Howard iteration
items.strategy: Compare successive policy equations through inverse positivity, obtain strict value increase at switched states, exclude repeated policies, and identify the stopping policy as a Bellman solution.

references.title: Wang He, Reinforcement Learning: A Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 10, Policy Improvement and Policy Iteration
references.locator: §§10.6–10.9: policy-improvement theorem, exact algorithm, and finite termination.

items.statement:
For exact policy evaluations, every strict switch in
[[alg-na-finite-control-howard-policy-iteration]] weakly increases the policy
value at every state and strictly increases it at each switched state. No
deterministic policy can recur after a strict switch. With budget
$P=\prod_i|A_i|$, the algorithm terminates within $P$ policy evaluations at
the unique solution of the Bellman system in
[[def-na-finite-state-discounted-bellman-system]]. A smaller budget may return
`budget_exhausted` without a solution claim.

items.title: Initial trace for the explicit diagonal-diffusion HJB scheme
items.strategy: Bound finite controlled random-walk displacement in second moment, then apply the common modulus of the initial data.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §6, initial-boundary conditions and half-relaxed stability; the local finite-step trace estimate is proved here.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, stability and initial-data hypotheses for monotone approximation schemes; the controlled random-walk bound is proved here.

items.statement:
Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and use the explicit diagonal-diffusion
scheme of [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] with mesh
widths $h_{k,j}\to0$, time steps $\tau_k\to0$, and its diffusion-dominance
and CFL inequalities at every row. Then for every sequence of integers
$n_k\ge0$ with $t_k=n_k\tau_k\to0$ and $t_k$ within the computed horizon,
$$\sup_i|U_i^{n_k}-u_0(x_i)|\longrightarrow0.$$
The estimate is uniform over all finite control choices generated by the
maximization in the scheme.

items.title: Nonnegative row weights for the diagonal-diffusion HJB stencil
items.strategy: Expand each control row and verify the center, both directional neighbors, and row sum under the stated dominance and CFL inequalities.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §1.2 and §1.6, degenerate ellipticity and controlled second-order operators, printed pp. 4–7.

items.statement:
Under the two inequalities in [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]],
every fixed-control row of its explicit update is an affine combination of the
center and the two coordinate neighbors with nonnegative coefficients summing
to one, plus $\tau f^a$. Therefore the max over controls is order-preserving.

items.title: Closed elliptic space-time jets test the parabolic diagonal HJB inequality
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions
references.locator: Section 2, equations (2.3), (2.6), Remark 2.4; Section 8, Remark 8.1.

items.statement:
Let $u$ be a USC viscosity subsolution in the sense of
[[def-na-second-order-parabolic-viscosity-solution]], and write the local
space-time variable as $z=(t,x)$. If
$((a,p),H)\in\overline J^{2,+}u(t,x)$ is a closed elliptic jet in all $d+1$
variables ([[def-na-second-order-elliptic-semijets-and-closure]]), and $X$ is the spatial
principal block of $H$, then
$$a-\max_{c\in A}\left\{\sum_j(\alpha_j^c(x,t)X_{jj}+b_j^c(x,t)p_j)+f^c(x,t)\right\}\le0.$$
For an LSC supersolution and a closed elliptic subjet the reverse inequality
holds. All points are interior in time; local periodic lifts are understood.

items.title: Initial trace for the positive-interpolation and upwind HJB schemes
items.strategy: Represent finite updates by finite controlled transition kernels and bound drift plus interpolation or upwind martingale variance near t=0.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §§2–4, positive interpolation transitions and semi-Lagrangian scheme, printed pp. 2–5.

references.locator: Chapter 1 §§4–6, stability, initial data, and comparison for the Cauchy problem, printed pp. 21–29.

items.statement:
Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and let $B$ and $L$ bound the drift and
running cost in [[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. For the semi-Lagrangian
scheme, if $t_n=n\tau\to0$, $h_{\max}\to0$, and
$h_{\max}^2/\tau\to0$, then
$$\sup_i|U_i^n-u_0(x_i)|\longrightarrow0.$$
For the upwind scheme, the same conclusion holds when $t_n\to0$,
$h_{\max}\to0$, and its CFL condition holds. Both statements are uniform over
all finite control policies and remain true for a finite control discretization.

items.title: Smooth test functions suffice for the first- and second-order HJB viscosity notions
items.strategy: Strictify a C1 or C1,2 contact without changing its relevant jet, mollify in C1 or C1,2 on a compact neighborhood, and pass the smooth-test inequality through the maximizing contacts.

references.title: Hung Vinh Tran, Hamilton–Jacobi Equations: Theory and Applications, 2020 author manuscript
references.locator: Chapter 1 §§1–2, test-function and viscosity definitions, printed pp. 15–22.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §2, test-function viscosity definitions and second-order parabolic conventions, printed pp. 9–13 and 49–50.

items.statement:
For the continuous first-order Hamiltonian of
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]], requiring the subsolution or
supersolution inequality only for smooth ($C^\infty$) local test functions is
equivalent to requiring it for all $C^1$ tests. For the diagonal second-order
operator of [[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]], the
same equivalence holds between smooth tests and all $C^{1,2}$ tests in
[[def-na-second-order-parabolic-viscosity-solution]]. The result is local in
space-time and applies to upper semicontinuous subsolutions and lower
semicontinuous supersolutions.

items.title: Smooth consistency of the diagonal-diffusion Bellman stencil
items.strategy: Taylor expand the central second differences, one-sided drift differences, and explicit time step with uniform coefficient bounds.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §2, Taylor consistency conditions for controlled diffusion stencils, printed pp. 2–3.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, test-function consistency requirement for second-order schemes, printed pp. 274–276.

items.statement:
Assume the coefficients are bounded and periodic and a periodic test function
$\phi$ is smooth with bounded derivatives $\phi_{tt}$, $\phi_{x_jx_j}$, and
$\phi_{x_jx_jx_jx_j}$, and the coefficients are bounded. For the scheme of
[[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]], define the normalized
local residual
$$R_{h,\tau}(x_i,t_n)=\frac{\phi(x_i,t_n+\tau)-S_{h,\tau}\phi(\cdot,t_n)_i}{\tau}.$$
Then
$$R_{h,\tau}=\phi_t-\max_{a\in A}\left\{ \sum_j(\alpha_j^a\phi_{x_jx_j}+b_j^a\phi_{x_j})+f^a\right\} +O\left(\tau+\max_j\left[\alpha_{j,\max}h_j^2\|\phi_{x_j^4}\|_\infty+ |b_j|_{\max}h_j\|\phi_{x_jx_j}\|_\infty\right]\right),$$
where $\alpha_{j,\max}:=\sup_{a,x,t}\alpha_j^a(x,t)$ and
$|b_j|_{\max}:=\sup_{a,x,t}|b_j^a(x,t)|$. The bound is uniform over nodes and
times before the terminal step. The $O(\cdot)$ is a
smooth-test residual estimate, not a solution-error rate.

items.title: Monotonicity, L-infinity stability, and consistency of the semi-Lagrangian HJB step
items.strategy: Use positive partition-of-unity weights for order and stability; Taylor expand the footpoint and time update for the O(dt+h²/dt) residual.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §§2–4, positive interpolation, first-order drift approximation, and LISL monotonicity, printed pp. 2–5.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, monotonicity and consistency assumptions for approximation schemes, printed pp. 274–276.

items.statement:
For the update $S_{h,\tau}$ of
[[alg-na-positive-interpolation-semilagrangian-hjb-step]], if $V\le W$ at all
nodes then $S_{h,\tau}V\le S_{h,\tau}W$. If $|\ell_a|\le L$, then
$$\|S_{h,\tau}V\|_\infty\le\|V\|_\infty+\tau L.$$
For $\phi\in C^2$ in space and time with bounded derivatives, on a compact
test region with $|D\phi|\le P$,
$$\frac{\phi(t_n+\tau,x_i)-S_{h,\tau}\phi(t_n,\cdot)_i}{\tau} =\phi_t(x_i,t_n)+H(x_i,t_n,D\phi(x_i,t_n)) +O\left(\tau+\frac{h_{\max}^2}{\tau}+\eta_k(P)\right).$$
The term $\eta_k(P)$ is zero when the full finite control set is used.

items.title: Monotonicity, L-infinity stability, and consistency of the upwind HJB step
items.strategy: Write each control row as a convex combination under the CFL condition, then use one-sided Taylor expansions for consistency.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §§6.5–6.6, explicit upwind row and smooth consistency, PDF pp. 97–104.

references.title: Hung Vinh Tran, Hamilton–Jacobi Equations: Theory and Applications, 2020 author manuscript
references.locator: Chapter 3 §4, monotone and consistent finite-difference schemes, printed pp. 100–103.

items.statement:
Assume the first-order HJB coefficients satisfy the hypotheses of
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. Under the CFL condition in
[[alg-na-upwind-hjb-grid-step]], each one-control update is a convex
combination of the current node and its one-sided neighbors plus
$\tau\ell_a$. Consequently the control-minimum update is order-preserving and
$$\|U^{n+1}\|_\infty\le\|U^n\|_\infty+\tau L.$$
For a smooth periodic test function $\phi$ with bounded derivatives through
order two, the normalized local residual satisfies
$$\frac{\phi(t_n+\tau,x_i)-S_{h,\tau}\phi(t_n,\cdot)_i}{\tau} =\phi_t(x_i,t_n)+H(x_i,t_n,D\phi(x_i,t_n))+O(\tau+h_{\max}+\eta_k(P)),$$
where $S_{h,\tau}$ is the scheme map, $h_{\max}=\max_jh_j$, $P$ bounds
$|D\phi|$ on the tested compact set, and $\eta_k(P)=0$ for exact control
minimization.

items.title: Half-relaxed limits of the monotone diagonal-diffusion HJB scheme
items.strategy: At local extrema of the half-relaxed limits, use the nonnegative stencil weights and smooth-test consistency; prove the initial trace from the same finite transition-kernel moment bound.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §6 stability of viscosity solutions and upper/lower relaxed limits; §8 parabolic test conventions, printed pp. 34–35 and 49–52.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, Theorem 2.1 proof: monotonicity, consistency, and grid-contact half-relaxed passage, printed pp. 274–276.

items.statement:
Let $h_{k,j}\to0$, $\tau_k=T/M_k\to0$, and let $U_k$ be the finite
solutions of [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] with its
diffusion-dominance and CFL inequalities at every row. Extend each array
multilinearly in space, constantly on each time interval, and by its initial
interpolant for $-1<t<0$; identify the mesh sequence with the parameter
family convention of [[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. Its upper
half-relaxed limit is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution,
and its lower half-relaxed limit is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity
supersolution of the periodic diagonal-diffusion Cauchy problem, with the
respective relaxed initial inequalities equal to $u_0$. This is a stability
statement only; it does not claim that the two limits coincide.

items.title: Convergence of the positive-interpolation and upwind first-order HJB schemes
items.strategy: Prove the mesh-node subsolution and supersolution inequalities by monotonicity and consistency, enforce the initial trace, and squeeze the periodic envelopes using the exact published comparison hypotheses.

references.title: Hung Vinh Tran, Hamilton–Jacobi Equations: Theory and Applications, 2020 author manuscript
references.locator: Chapter 3 §4, Theorem 3.15 and the grid-maximum proof for monotone consistent schemes, printed pp. 100–103.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, assumptions (2.2)–(2.5), Theorem 2.1 and proof, printed pp. 274–276.

references.title: Kristian Debrabant and Espen R. Jakobsen, Semi-Lagrangian schemes for linear and fully non-linear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations
references.locator: §§2–4, positive interpolation and first-order semi-Lagrangian HJB update, printed pp. 2–5.

items.statement:
Let $u_0$ and the coefficients satisfy
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. Consider a sequence of periodic
grids with $h_{k,\max}\to0$, time steps $\tau_k=T/M_k\to0$, $M_k\in\mathbb N$,
and finite nonempty control sets $A_k\subseteq A$ whose Hamiltonian errors
$\eta_k(R)$ tend to zero for each finite $R$. For the positive-interpolation
scheme additionally assume $h_{k,\max}^2/\tau_k\to0$. For the upwind scheme
assume its CFL condition at every step. Extend the initial interpolant
constantly for $-1<t<0$ and identify the mesh sequence with the parameter
family $V_\epsilon=V_k$ for $(k+1)^{-1}<\epsilon\le k^{-1}$ in
[[def-half-relaxed-limits]]. Then the respective piecewise
multilinear-in-space, piecewise-constant-in-time extensions of the nodal
solutions converge locally uniformly on $\mathbb T^d\times[0,T)$ to the same
bounded continuous viscosity solution of the Cauchy problem. This conclusion
includes exact finite-control models ($A_k=A$), where $\eta_k=0$. The proof
does not assert a rate.

items.title: Comparison for periodic diagonal controlled-diffusion HJB equations
items.strategy: contradiction
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the exact finite-control coefficient hypotheses of
[[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]], in any dimension
$d\ge1$. Let $u$ be bounded upper semicontinuous and $v$ bounded lower
semicontinuous on $\mathbb T^d\times(0,T)$; assume their interior
$C^{1,2}$-test inequalities are those of
[[def-na-second-order-parabolic-viscosity-solution]], using the local
maximum/minimum contact convention of
[[def-viscosity-subsolution-and-supersolution]]. Suppose the raw relaxed initial
traces are ordered at every $x\in\mathbb T^d$:
$$\limsup_{\substack{(y,t)\to(x,0)\\t>0}}u(y,t)\le\liminf_{\substack{(y,t)\to(x,0)\\t>0}}v(y,t).$$
Then $u\le v$ on $\mathbb T^d\times(0,T)$. In particular this applies to the
model's common continuous initial datum and its two relaxed initial
inequalities. Defining the values at $t=0$ by their respective raw upper and
lower envelopes gives the same order there. No continuity, spatial Lipschitz
bound, or differentiability of $u,v$ is assumed.

references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.7 and Example 3.6; Section 8, Remark 8.1 and proof of Theorem 8.2.

items.title: Conditional convergence of the diagonal-diffusion scheme under comparison
items.strategy: Assume comparison for the exact second-order coefficient class, identify both half-relaxed limits, and rule out failure of uniform convergence on the compact periodic cylinder.

references.title: Guy Barles and Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: §2, Theorem 2.1 and proof: comparison squeezes upper/lower relaxed limits to a continuous limit, printed pp. 274–276.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §6, stability and comparison route for half-relaxed limits, printed pp. 34–35.

items.statement:
For a sequence of diagonal-diffusion grid schemes satisfying the hypotheses
of [[thm-na-diagonal-diffusion-scheme-half-relaxed-limits]], suppose in
addition that the exact periodic Cauchy problem
[[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]] has a comparison
principle for bounded upper semicontinuous subsolutions and bounded lower
semicontinuous supersolutions with ordered relaxed initial traces. Then the
upper and lower half-relaxed limits coincide, define the unique bounded
continuous viscosity solution, and the spatially interpolated numerical
solutions converge locally uniformly on $\mathbb T^d\times[0,T)$ to it.
This corollary is conditional on the stated second-order comparison property;
it does not supply or assert that property.

items.title: Unconditional convergence and existence for the periodic diagonal-diffusion HJB scheme
items.strategy: direct

references.title: Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions
references.locator: Section 6, Remark 6.4; Section 8, comparison and initial data.

references.title: Barles and Souganidis, Convergence of approximation schemes for fully nonlinear second order equations
references.locator: Section 2, Theorem 2.1, comparison and half-relaxed squeezing.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For the full model of
[[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]], let
$h_{k,j}=1/N_{k,j}\to0$, $N_{k,j}\ge3$, and $\tau_k=T/M_k\to0$.
Assume the explicit scheme
[[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] satisfies its
diffusion-dominance and CFL inequalities at every row, and initialize it by
$U_{k,i}^0=u_0(x_{k,i})$. Its multilinear-in-space, constant-on-time-interval
extensions converge locally uniformly on $\mathbb T^d\times[0,T)$ to the
unique bounded continuous viscosity solution of the model Cauchy problem.
Such admissible mesh sequences exist for every model in this coefficient
class, so the conclusion also proves existence of that viscosity solution.
Comparison and uniqueness apply among all bounded continuous viscosity
solutions with the prescribed initial trace. There is no additional
comparison hypothesis and no claimed solution-error rate.

title: Monotone Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman schemes and policy iteration — Examples

items.title: A centered HJB update can fail monotonicity
items.strategy: Use nonnegative periodic data supported at one neighbor to make the centered update negative at the adjacent state.

references.title: Hung Vinh Tran, Hamilton–Jacobi Equations: Theory and Applications, 2020 author manuscript
references.locator: Chapter 3 §4, monotone finite-difference schemes and the role of positive stencil weights, printed pp. 100–103.

references.title: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations
references.locator: §§6.5–6.6, centered versus upwind treatment of advection stencils, PDF pp. 97–104.

items.statement:
On a periodic one-dimensional grid with $N\ge3$, $h=1/N$, and controls
$A=\{-1,1\}$, replace the upwind derivative in the HJB equation
$u_t=\min_{a\in A}a u_x$ by the centered derivative and define
$$S_c(V)_i=V_i+\tau\min_{a\in\{-1,1\}} a\frac{V_{i+1}-V_{i-1}}{2h}.$$
This map is not order-preserving: there are arrays $U\le V$ with
$S_c(U)_i>S_c(V)_i$.

items.title: A two-state switching example for discounted Howard iteration
items.strategy: Solve a two-state, two-action discounted generator system exactly and verify a strict policy switch, tie retention, and the final Bellman equation.

references.locator: §1, controlled HJB operators and finite-control conventions, printed pp. 1–2.

items.statement:
Take states $S=\{1,2\}$ and discount $c=1$. At state $1$ the ordered actions
are `stay`, with generator row $(q_{11},q_{12})=(0,0)$ and reward $0$, then
`go`, with row $(-1,1)$ and reward $0$. At state $2$ the ordered actions are
`exit`, `tied-exit`, and `reset`, with rows respectively $(q_{21},q_{22})=(0,0)$,
$(0,0)$, and $(1,-1)$, and rewards $2,2,0$. The least-index initial policy
is `(stay, exit)`. Howard iteration makes one strict switch at state $1$,
retains `exit` at state `2` despite its tie, and terminates with value
$V=(1,2)$.

items.title: A periodic manufactured solution for the diagonal-diffusion HJB stencil
items.strategy: Choose a smooth periodic trigonometric solution, derive its forcing exactly, and compute the discrete residual and its vanishing mesh limit.

references.title: Michael G. Crandall, Hitoshi Ishii, and Pierre-Louis Lions, User's guide to viscosity solutions of second order partial differential equations
references.locator: §1.6, controlled-diffusion HJB operator and degenerate-elliptic sign convention.

items.statement:
For $d=1$, one control, $\alpha=1$, and $b=0$ on $\mathbb T^1$, set
$$u(x,t)=e^{-t}\cos(2\pi x),\qquad f(x,t)=(-1+4\pi^2)e^{-t}\cos(2\pi x).$$
Then $u_t-(u_{xx}+f)=0$ exactly. On a periodic grid $h=1/N$, the centered
diffusion scheme with $0<\tau\le h^2/2$ satisfies a normalized one-step
residual of order $O(\tau+h^2)$ on the sampled exact solution. This is a
local residual calculation, not a global solution-error estimate.

items.title: Uniform Hamiltonian error for an evenly spaced compact-control grid
items.strategy: For a scalar compact control interval, compute the exact Hamiltonian and bound the uniform error of an evenly spaced finite action grid on bounded momentum sets.

items.statement:
Let $A=[-1,1]$, $b(a)=a$, and $\ell(a)=a^2$. Then
$$H(p)=\max_{a\in[-1,1]}(-ap-a^2)= \begin{cases} p^2/4,&|p|\le2,\\ |p|-1,&|p|>2. \end{cases}$$
For $m\ge1$, let $A_m=\{-1+2r/m:r=0,\ldots,m\}$ and let
$H_m(p)=\max_{a\in A_m}(-ap-a^2)$. The uniform control-grid error satisfies
$$\sup_{p\in\mathbb R}|H_m(p)-H(p)|\le m^{-2}.$$
Thus $A_m$ satisfies the control approximation hypothesis of
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. For any continuous periodic initial
datum, its semi-Lagrangian scheme falls under
[[thm-na-first-order-hjb-scheme-convergence]] whenever the stated mesh
restrictions also hold.

items.statement:
On $\mathbb T^1$, take $A=\{-1,1\}$, $b(a)=a$, $\ell=0$, so
$H(p)=|p|$. Let $d_{\mathbb T^1}(x,0)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|x-k|$ and
$$u(x,t)=\max\{d_{\mathbb T^1}(x,0)-t,0\},\qquad 0\le t\le1/4.$$
This is the viscosity solution of $u_t+|u_x|=0$ with initial data
$u_0(x)=d_{\mathbb T^1}(x,0)$. On a grid with an even number $N\ge4$ of
nodes, $h=1/N$, and $0$ a node, one step with $0<\tau\le h$ gives both the positive-interpolation
and upwind schemes value $\tau$ at $x=0$, whereas the exact solution there is
$0$. On the horizon $T=1/4$, choosing $M=N/2$ gives $\tau=T/M=h/2$; along
this even-grid family the one-step error is exactly $\tau$ and the
positive-interpolation mesh condition is satisfied.
